"Do you want a drink?" As a 22 y/o, extremely sociable, recovering alcoholic; I get this one a lot, and it never gets easier.
Congratulations on being able to place the word 'recovering' in front of alcoholic. Keep up the good work, this Internet stranger is rooting for you.
This actually made me far more emotional than I expected an internet comment to make me. Thank you!
First of all: Keep it up! If I may ask, when and how did you realise that you had a serious problem?

Of course you can ask!

It was about 3 months ago. I realized the amount I drank and how well I was able to hold it was not normal compared to all of my friends. Particularly how I was drinking. I have not, in a VERY long time, casually drank a drink. I down each and every drink I have, be it wine, spirits, cider, ANYTHING, I will gulp as much of it as I can, as quickly as I can. And once I have one, it's like something else takes over all all other priorities go out the window, all that matters is the next drink. I frequently steal unattended drinks (which is not only a dick move but also really dangerous) and down them and leave. Luckily, none of the drinks I took were ever drugged, but even if they were I probably wouldn't have noticed because each and every night had a blackout period.

My hangovers were a big tell too, I was always the most hungover, I don't remember the last time I had a drink without throwing up the next day. As I said, I frequently had blackouts, and I always thought this was normal, but I did my research and discovered it was not. Normal drinkers rarely if ever completely black out and wake up unaware of what has happened.

I spoke to a lot of alcoholics online, many whose lives had been completely ruined by their addiction. Almost all said that they had started out like this, and when I really thought about it I had noticed myself drinking more and more often. Every time something went wrong in my relationship? Drink. Confrontation with a friend? Drink. Feel bad about my weight? Drink. Watching a movie? Drink.

It was a huge wake up call. I don't want this, which clearly is a problem, has all the warning signs of completely fucking up my life, to actually fuck up my life. I ain't letting no god damn LIQUID control me! Fuck that shit.

I do miss it, and I do wish I was able to drink in moderation and be normal like all my friends. But I have tried, and I have not been able to succeed. I've blown rent money a week before rent day. I've cracked my skull. I've gotten into a fights (which is really against my nature). No more. That's the worst this shit is ever going to be. Fuck that.

edit : formatting

edit 2: But there was no moment I realized I had a problem, but there was a major moment when I accepted I had a problem. That was a tough day. I still can't accept the fact that I can't ever drink, but taking it day by day, party by party, and saying "I'm staying sober tonight" is much easier. It took me a long time to finally kick it and stop drinking. But I'm sober a month now and attending therapy & AA meetings every week. Things have got a lot better, in my romantic relationship, and my relationship with my family. I was never aggressive, but since becoming sober I am much calmer and understanding of other people, and I have no idea how that happened, but I'm glad I did.

Wrangler (YJ): Should I keep it and upgrade it or run it into the ground?

I would say put the money in if you like the look and function and it fits your needs as a family. If you need to replace the shocks and struts that's not too much I'm sure but if the engine and tranny run well and there's no rust it seems the major things are working well so you should be able to avoid sinking major money into this.

IMHO, YJ must be a labor of love at this point. It will spend weeks in the shop and you must have a reliable vehicle to back it up.
